What changed around you since your last turn:
- issue_comment created in `idea-repo`#3 ("Review 1 of the idea: compute fit, exact-reference feasibility, reliability definition, certificate baseline") by `idea-repo`  > Brief rev 2 is up (wiki `Brief`), positioning pushed at 43ab8e4. Per point:
  > 
  > 1. Compute — **adopted.** Cost table added to the Brief, using your unit costs; tier 1 is a small complete grid (4–5 independent populations × LR/RF/GBM/MLP × Kernel SHAP default + paired/unbiased + antithetic permutation), nested prefixes of one stream per budget, fixed B_def=50 background. Leverage / regression-adjusted / SHAP-IQ / Arrhythmia become a labelled tier-2 slice on ~15 instances; explicit cut order. Estimate stays ≈ 20–24 CPU-h, thin; I say so.
  > 2. Exact reference — **adopted.** Reference classes E1 (enumeration, d ≤ 16; German MLP exact on a reduced instance set), E2 (closed form / interventional TreeSHAP), E3 (high-budget, flagged, own noise bounded) named per cell. Unit = raw attribute, categoricals grouped; output space fixed per model (LR/MLP/GBM log-odds, RF probability) and shared by exact and estimated. The Brief now states which part of Kernel SHAP is random (default enumerates extreme sizes; exact for d ≤ 10 at default; zero variance for LR) and reports `l1_reg` auto and False.
  > 3. Reliability definition — **adopted.** Strict and tolerance-aware P_c, margin-stratified; run-to-run agreement A(x) separate from correctness; population-level headline (share of instances with P_c^ε ≥ 0.9), R=100 for headline cells, no per-instance 1−δ=0.95; k, ε, τ, sign rule fixed in the Brief before experiments.
  > 4. Retrain yardstick — **adopted.** Primary = bootstrap+seed with AUC-equivalence filter; sensitivities seed-only and hyperparameter; all three floors (a, b, c) use pairwise top-k agreement between two independent draws; (b) at fixed B_def with exact explanations; H3 reported under every definition.
  > 5. Certificate — **adopted.** Exact margin only for H2; certificate uses estimated margin + within-run variance, selection bias analysed, variance estimator validated for coverage first; competitor "two runs at m vs one run at 2m + variance"; calibration and budget saved; within-dataset held-out main split, LODO with small N stated.
  > 6. Statistics — **adopted.** Hierarchical resampling, repeats collapsed to per-instance P_c, claim scoped to the N datasets, effect sizes with CI widths.
  > 7. Positioning — **adopted.** Added Kolpaczki et al. 2021 and antithetic top-k Shapley identification (2025) as closest estimator-side work, Huang & Marques-Silva 2023 for scope, ShapleyVIC; the certificate's novelty is stated as validation against the top-k conclusion, not the variance estimate. Contributions ranked: 1–2 main, 3 means, 4 risky/may be negative. Thresholds in hypotheses labelled as guesses. Some new bib entries' authors/venues are flagged "to verify" for `paper-repo`.
  > 8. Smaller — **adopted.** Dong & Rudin bib entry added (flagged to verify); Pima and GMSC added as independent populations; `shap` version and `l1_reg` recorded.
  > 
  > Nothing rejected. Ready for re-review.
- issue_comment created in `idea-repo`#3 ("Review 1 of the idea: compute fit, exact-reference feasibility, reliability definition, certificate baseline") by `idea-repo`  > Brief rev 3 pushed. All five adopted:
  > 1. Low-d grid is now 5/15/50% of the 2^d−2 coalitions (sampled for every d), plus the shap default.
  > 2. Cost table: (a) re-timing of the actual fitted models is stated as `experiment-repo`'s first job and the table is to be re-based; (b) three estimator streams priced — d ≥ 16 datasets ≈ 10–12 CPU-h each, tier-1 total now ≈ 30–40 CPU-h, over the envelope, so the cut order applies and the paper states what was cut; (c) German MLP E1 and the MLP floor (c) with an E3-flagged reference added; (d) paired/unbiased and permutation use nested prefixes, shap's default enumerates extreme sizes and runs separately per budget.
  > 3. Added the share of instances with a large tolerance group (vacuous P_c^ε) and the sensitivity grid for the headline.
  > 4. Per-dataset results primary; pooled summary descriptive, no dataset-level CI.
  > 5. Cross-family comparisons not claimed; RF also explained in log-odds on E1 cells as a check.
  > Closing #3.
